target.title: fix(line): record every LINE push message id in send receipts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LINE send receipts discarded all returned LINE message ids and mislabeled multi-part sends. `pushLineMessages` returned a hardcoded `messageId: "push"` and `sendMessageLine`'s reply branch returned `"reply"` while discarding the response, so neither path recorded a real id. A single send can produce several messages — media + caption is two, one `sentMessages[].id` each — and every returned id was dropped from the receipt. The receipt also stamped one aggregate `kind` on every id, recording a media + caption send as `[media, media]` instead of `[media, text]`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`@line/bot-sdk` 11.1.0 types the `sentMessages` response as 1–5 items (`minItems: 1`), one per submitted message, for both push (`PushMessageResponse`) and reply (`ReplyMessageResponse`), and LINE guarantees the array order matches the sent message objects ([LINE docs](https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/get-quote-tokens/): "the order of the elements in the `sentMessages` array is guaranteed to be the same as the order of the message objects when they were sent"). Push discarded that response; reply never captured it. Because a successful response carries at least one id (`minItems: 1`), the removed `"push"` / `"reply"` were placeholders, not ids; handling a malformed empty response is separate hardening and out of scope.

Push and reply now share one ordered receipt path (`buildLineSendResult`): the first returned id stays the singular `messageId`, every id is recorded as an ordered `parts` entry, and each id is keyed to its own kind via the documented order (`sentMessages[i]` ↔ `messages[i]`), so a media + caption send records `[media, text]`. Both paths share the same broken receipt invariant; recording ids without their kinds, or fixing one path and not the other, leaves the receipt half-correct, so they land together.

The per-message kind rides a small additive `kinds?` parameter on the shared receipt normalizer (`createMessageReceiptFromOutboundResults`), applied by index to single-part flat results only. The normalizer already owns id-dedup, primary-id derivation, and part/`sentAt` assembly and only accepted one uniform `kind`; the alternative — LINE building the `MessageReceipt` itself — would fork all of that assembly into the plugin and drift from the shared shape. The additive parameter instead keeps one receipt builder, touches no existing caller (uniform-`kind` callers and nested-receipt adapters are unchanged), and adds no new receipt shape (`platformMessageIds`, `parts`, `primaryPlatformMessageId` already model ordered multi-id receipts); "one physical message carries its own kind" is a generic receipt property, not LINE-specific.

Scope (5 files): LINE response capture + receipt construction (`send.ts`, `send-receipt.ts`), one additive core normalizer option (`receipt.ts`), and the two focused test files.

## User Impact

Consumers of LINE send receipts get the real LINE message id for every sent message, on push and on reply. The receipt schema is unchanged: `messageId` / `primaryPlatformMessageId` change value (real id instead of a `"push"` / `"reply"` placeholder), and `platformMessageIds` / `parts` change cardinality — a media + caption send now exposes both ordered ids (one `parts` entry each) with kinds `[media, text]`.

## Evidence

**Tests** — `pnpm test extensions/line` (26 files, 310 tests passed) and `pnpm test src/channels/message/receipt.test.ts` pass. A media + caption reply asserts both ids in order with kinds `[media, text]` and the first primary; the media + caption push asserts the same order plus `parts[].kind === [media, text]`; a normalizer case asserts per-result `kinds` apply by index with aggregate-kind fallback. `tsgo`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are clean; GitHub CI is green on this head.

**Manual credential-backed proof** — a `node --import tsx` script drives the production `sendMessageLine` path against the real LINE Messaging API with a real channel access token, for a media + caption send LINE delivers as two messages, on both push and reply (reply token captured live from an inbound webhook event). For each path it asserts `platformMessageIds` equals both returned ids in order, `messageId`/`primaryPlatformMessageId` equals the first, and — via LINE's documented `sentMessages` order — `parts[].kind` equals `[media, text]`; both pass against real numeric LINE ids. Reverting the `send.ts` mapping reproduces the `"push"`/`"reply"` placeholder.

## Summary

- Problem: The `exec-wrapper-tokens.ts` module normalizes executable tokens for wrapper/policy matching but lacked test coverage, risking silent regression in cross-platform path handling.
- Root cause: No test file existed for `basenameLower` and `normalizeExecutableToken`.
- Fix: Add 9 unit tests covering POSIX paths, Windows paths, suffix stripping (.exe/.cmd/.bat/.com), non-executable extensions, and edge cases.
- Out of scope: No source changes; test-only addition.

## Linked context

Tests `src/infra/exec-wrapper-tokens.ts` — no linked issue (test gap fill).

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: `basenameLower` returns lowercase basename; `normalizeExecutableToken` strips executable suffixes (.exe/.cmd/.bat/.com) and lowercases the result.
- Real environment tested: Windows 10, Node.js v22.22.3, production functions from `src/infra/exec-wrapper-tokens.js`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: imported the production module via `node --import tsx -e` and called `basenameLower`/`normalizeExecutableToken` with representative inputs
- Evidence after fix:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import('./src/infra/exec-wrapper-tokens.js').then(({basenameLower,normalizeExecutableToken})=>console.log(JSON.stringify([{f:'basenameLower',i:'/usr/bin/Node',r:basenameLower('/usr/bin/Node')},{f:'normalizeExecutableToken',i:'node.exe',r:normalizeExecutableToken('node.exe')},{f:'normalizeExecutableToken',i:'C:\\Program Files\\node.exe',r:normalizeExecutableToken('C:\\Program Files\\node.exe')},{f:'normalizeExecutableToken',i:'script.cmd',r:normalizeExecutableToken('script.cmd')},{f:'normalizeExecutableToken',i:'config.json',r:normalizeExecutableToken('config.json')}])))"
[{"f":"basenameLower","i":"/usr/bin/Node","r":"node"},{"f":"normalizeExecutableToken","i":"node.exe","r":"node"},{"f":"normalizeExecutableToken","i":"C:\\Program Files\\node.exe","r":"node"},{"f":"normalizeExecutableToken","i":"script.cmd","r":"script"},{"f":"normalizeExecutableToken","i":"config.json","r":"config.json"}]

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/exec-wrapper-tokens.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

- Observed result after fix: All 9 tests pass; `normalizeExecutableToken` correctly strips .exe/.cmd suffixes and lowercases; `basenameLower` correctly extracts and lowercases basename from POSIX and Windows paths.
- What was not tested: Live cross-platform exec wrapper matching (requires runtime process spawn).

## Regression test plan

- Config/env/migration changed? No
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-exec changed? No

target.title: fix(agents): classify account-restricted model 400s as model_not_found
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an embedded Codex run fails because the configured model is not available on the account/plan (HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`: *"The 'gpt-5.5-pro' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."*), Telegram users get the generic *"Something went wrong… try again, or use /new"* copy (#104490). Retrying or `/new` cannot fix a model/account mismatch — the actionable cause was only visible in gateway logs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause is a classification gap, not missing copy. The pipeline for this failure already exists end to end:

1. The ambiguous-400 branch in `classifyFailoverSignal` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`) explicitly inspects the payload first "so … model-not-found errors … are not collapsed into generic format failures" — but `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` (`src/agents/live-model-errors.ts`) had no pattern for the account-restricted rejection sentence, so the error fell through to `format`.
2. With a `model_not_found` reason, the assistant-failover layer already does the right things: tries configured fallback models, and when surfacing throws a typed `FailoverError`.
3. `classifyProviderRequestError` already maps that typed reason to `PROVIDER_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_USER_MESSAGE` — copy that matches the issue's expectation ("needs a config update…; retrying or starting a new session won't fix it").

The fix is one pattern in the classifier that owns model-error text: `model … is not supported when using …`. The "when using" qualifier keeps capability rejections ("This model is not supported for tool calling.") out of the class — the existing negative tests still pass. No change to `classifyProviderRequestError`: its "typed reason only, no text matching" contract from #97611 is preserved (the message-level classification happens in the failover layer that owns it).

The issue's admin-notification request (route sanitized diagnostics to an operator) is a separate product surface and intentionally not part of this fix.

## User Impact

- Telegram (and every channel using the shared failure-reply path) now shows: *"⚠️ The configured model is unavailable from the provider — it may have been renamed, retired, or is not offered on this account. This needs a config update (agents.defaults.model); retrying or starting a new session won't fix it."* instead of the misleading retry//new suggestion.
- With fallback models configured, the run now fails over to the next model instead of dying on a `format`-classified error.

## Evidence

**Executed real-module before/after** (tsx over the actual source chain — failover classification → surfaced `FailoverError` → user-copy classification — using the exact payload from the issue's logs):

Before (main):
```
stage1 failover reason: "format"
stage2 classification code: (none)
USER SEES: ⚠️ Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again, or use /new to start a fresh session.
```

After (this PR):
```
stage1 failover reason: "model_not_found"
stage2 classification code: provider_model_unavailable
USER SEES: ⚠️ The configured model is unavailable from the provider — it may have been renamed, retired, or is not offered on this account. This needs a config update (agents.defaults.model); retrying or starting a new session won't fix it.
```

Both runs include the capability-rejection guard: `"This model is not supported for tool calling."` stays **out** of `model_not_found` before and after.

**Regression tests** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/live-model-errors.test.ts src/agents/failover-error.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/provider-request-error-classifier.test.ts` → 122/122):

- `live-model-errors.test.ts`: the issue sentence and its raw JSON envelope both classify as model-not-found; existing negatives (capability/feature rejections) unchanged.
- `failover-error.test.ts`: `status: 400` + the Codex payload resolves to `model_not_found`; capability 400s do not.
- Reverting only `live-model-errors.ts` fails both new tests (2 failed | 97 passed), confirming they gate the fix.

Codex-side provenance: the sibling `openai/codex` checkout confirms this rejection is generated by the OpenAI backend and forwarded verbatim (`codex-rs/core/tests/suite/compact.rs` mocks it as an HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`; `codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs` `UnexpectedResponseError` carries the body through), so message-level classification on the OpenClaw side is the right seam.

Fixes #104490

target.title: [AI] fix(feishu): send text and voice separately for Auto-TTS replies
target.body:
## Summary

**What problem does this PR solve?**

Feishu Auto-TTS 语音回复完全抑制文本内容，用户只能看到音频气泡，无法阅读文本回复。这与 WhatsApp/Discord 等其他 channel 的行为不一致。

**Why does this matter now?**

Issue #103509：用户在使用 Feishu Auto-TTS 功能时，无法阅读文本内容，只能看到音频气泡，严重影响用户体验。

**What is the intended outcome?**

用户可以阅读文本消息（第一条）+ 听语音回复（第二条），两者独立，不重复。

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- No changes to core TTS supplement contract
- No changes to other channel implementations
- No user configuration or API changes
- No new dependencies

**What does success look like?**

- Feishu Auto-TTS replies show text + voice as separate messages
- All existing tests pass (195 passed)
- Backward compatible with native voice-only payloads

**What should reviewers focus on?**

- Core logic: `extensions/feishu/src/media.ts:720-758` (shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia)
- Integration: `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:670-678` (ttsSupplement handling)
- Tests: `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts:229-263` (3 new test cases)

## Change Type

- **Severity**: P2
- **Type**: Bug fix
- **Size**: M (+140 prod, −4 prod, +71 test)

## Scope

**Files changed**:
```
extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts    | 38 ++++++++++++++++++
extensions/feishu/src/media.ts         | 14 +++++++
extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts | 71 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-
extensions/feishu/src/outbound.ts      | 16 +++++++-
src/channels/plugins/outbound.types.ts |  4 +-
5 files changed, 140 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

**What did NOT change**:
- Core TTS supplement contract (`src/auto-reply/reply-payload.ts`)
- Other channel implementations (Discord, WhatsApp, Matrix)
- User configuration or CLI commands
- Plugin SDK boundaries

## Motivation

**Real behavior proof**: See Evidence section below

**Root Cause**: Feishu did not use TTS supplement metadata to distinguish between:
- TTS supplement voice (needs text + voice)
- Native voice-only payload (should not send text, preserve semantics)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Feishu Auto-TTS replies suppress all text content, users only see audio bubble.

**Real environment tested**: Unit tests cover all logic branches with deterministic fixtures.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix**:

Test results (JSON format):
```json
{
  "extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts": "47 passed (+3 new tests)",
  "extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts": "62 passed (+2 new tests)",
  "extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts": "86 passed",
  "src/plugin-sdk/reply-payload.test.ts": "56 passed"
}
```

New test coverage:
```typescript
// extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts:229-263
it("suppresses text for TTS supplement when text already delivered", () => {
  expect(shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia({
    mediaUrl: "https://example.com/tts.mp3",
    audioAsVoice: true,
    ttsSupplement: { spokenText: "...", visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: true }
  })).toBe(true);  // ✅ Text already sent via streaming
});

it("does not suppress text for TTS supplement when text not yet delivered", () => {
  expect(shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia({
    mediaUrl: "https://example.com/tts.mp3",
    audioAsVoice: true,
    ttsSupplement: { spokenText: "...", visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: false }
  })).toBe(false);  // ✅ Fresh TTS reply, send text + voice
});
```

**Observed result after fix**: 
- TTS supplement with `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: false` → sends text + voice separately
- TTS supplement with `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: true` → only sends voice
- Native voice media without ttsSupplement → maintains voice-only semantics

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu environment (requires Feishu developer account and test bot configuration)

**Proof limitations**: Deterministic unit tests only, not live Feishu execution

**Before evidence**: 
```typescript
// Before: Unconditional suppression for audioAsVoice: true
export function shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia(params: {
  audioAsVoice?: boolean;
}): boolean {
  if (params.audioAsVoice === true) {
    return true;  // ❌ Suppresses ALL audioAsVoice text
  }
}
```

## Root Cause Analysis

**问题代码**（定位到具体行）:
```typescript
// extensions/feishu/src/media.ts:719-744 (before fix)
export function shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia(params: {
  mediaUrl?: string;
  fileName?: string;
  contentType?: string;
  audioAsVoice?: boolean;
}): boolean {
  if (params.audioAsVoice === true) {
    return true;  // ❌ Unconditional suppression
  }
  // ... other detection logic
}
```

**根因**:
1. Feishu **completely did not import or use** `getReplyPayloadTtsSupplement` or `isReplyPayloadTtsSupplement`
2. Cannot distinguish whether `audioAsVoice: true` comes from:
   - TTS supplement payload (needs to send text)
   - Native voice-only payload (should not send text)
3. Results in ALL `audioAsVoice: true` audio suppressing text, including TTS supplement scenarios

**数据流分析**:
```
speech-core/tts.ts → markReplyPayloadAsTtsSupplement(payload)
                   ↓
                   payload.ttsSupplement = { spokenText, visibleTextAlreadyDelivered }
                   ↓
Feishu reply-dispatcher → ❌ Does not read payload.ttsSupplement
                        ↓
                        shouldSuppressFeishuTextForVoiceMedia({ audioAsVoice: true })
                        ↓
                        return true  // ❌ Unconditional suppression
```

**修复**:
```typescript
// extensions/feishu/src/media.ts:726-733 (after fix)
if (params.ttsSupplement?.spokenText) {
  // Only suppress if text already delivered; otherwise send both
  return params.ttsSupplement.visibleTextAlreadyDelivered === true;
}
```

## Security Impact

- **Secrets / Auth / Network / Tool execution changed?** No
- No security-related changes

## Best-fix Verdict

**Why this fix is correct**:
1. Uses existing TTS supplement contract (no new mechanism)
2. Precise control via `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered` flag (no duplication)
3. Maintains backward compatibility (native voice-only unchanged)
4. Matches other channels (Discord/WhatsApp/Matrix strategies)

**Alternative considered**:
- ❌ Remove all suppression → breaks native voice-only semantics
- ❌ Use audioAsVoice/file extension only → too broad, lacks precision
- ❌ Create new mechanism → duplicates existing contract

**Minimal surgery**: 
- Added 1 parameter to existing function
- Added 3 priority-based conditions
- Updated 2 integration points (dispatcher + adapter)
- No refactoring

## Compatibility

- **Backward compatible?** Yes
- **Migration needed?** No
- **Breaking changes to API/CLI?** No

## AI Assistance

- **Model**: Claude Sonnet 5
- **Author confirmation**: 作者已确认理解修复逻辑
- **Untested items**: Live Feishu execution (requires developer account)

## Tests and validation

**Which commands did you run?**
```bash
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts --run
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts --run
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts --run
pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/reply-payload.test.ts --run
```

**测试命名规范**（测试名即 bug 镜像）:
```typescript
// ✅ Good: Test name describes the bug fix
"suppresses text for TTS supplement when text already delivered"
"does not suppress text for TTS supplement when text not yet delivered"
"sends text and voice separately for TTS supplement when text not yet delivered"
```

**What regression coverage was added or updated?**
- 3 new unit tests in `media.test.ts` covering TTS supplement scenarios
- 2 new integration tests in `outbound.test.ts` covering text + voice separation
- Total: 5 new tests covering all boundary conditions

**What failed before this fix, if known?**
Feishu Auto-TTS replies showed only audio bubble, no readable text.

**If no test was added, why not?**
N/A — regression tests added.

## Risk checklist

**Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes
- Feishu Auto-TTS users can now read text messages alongside voice replies

**Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** No

**Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** No

**Highest-risk area**:
- Edge case where `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered` flag might be incorrectly set by streaming/block delivery

**Risk mitigation**:
- Flag is set automatically by core TTS pipeline (not manual)
- All existing tests pass (backward compatible)
- Fallback: if flag is missing, defaults to not suppressing (safe default)

## Current review state

**What is the next action?**
- Maintainer / ClawSweeper review

**What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?**
- ClawSweeper automated review (in progress)
- Maintainer review

**Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?**
- N/A — no bot comments yet

## Related items

- Issue: #103509
- Related PR: #82935 (TTS supplement contract introduction)
- Reference implementations:
  - Discord: `extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.ts:111-134`
  - WhatsApp: `extensions/whatsapp/src/send.ts:252-262`
  - Matrix: `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/send.ts:305-366`

target.title: feat: MCP Apps (ui://) Phase 0 — generic host in Control UI + plugin-declared MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

Adds Phase 0 support for the MCP Apps extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`) to OpenClaw's generic bundle MCP client and Control UI. Any configured MCP server can bind a tool to a `ui://` resource through `_meta.ui.resourceUri`; no server-specific host integration is required.

The official Excalidraw MCP App server is the conformance target. The external proof-of-concept plugin remains out of tree at [fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin).

## What changed

### Generic MCP Apps runtime

- Declares the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` client capability for `text/html;profile=mcp-app`.
- Parses nested and legacy flat `_meta.ui` declarations and reads bound `ui://` resources after successful tool calls.
- Filters app-only tools (`_meta.ui.visibility` without `model`) from agent exposure.
- Preserves the normal text/structured tool result for non-UI surfaces.

### Durable, bounded view storage

- Stores complete app view snapshots outside transcripts in the shared OpenClaw state SQLite database.
- Persists only an opaque, validated descriptor in `details.mcpApp`; app HTML, tool input, and tool result do not inflate `chat.history`.
- Enforces 30-day retention, 128 views, 256 MiB total, and 8 MiB per payload, including all persisted string fields.
- Physically deletes expired rows during lookup and prunes oldest rows on insertion.
- Invalid, expired, or evicted descriptors fail closed.

### Production Control UI host

- Resolves descriptors through a ticket-protected, no-store Gateway resource endpoint.
- Uses the MCP Apps double-frame sandbox pattern: an opaque-origin outer proxy and a nested `allow-scripts allow-same-origin` app frame.
- Applies the app-declared CSP in the proxy response and does not delegate camera, microphone, geolocation, or clipboard permissions.
- Renders the app inline even while the enclosing tool disclosure is collapsed.
- Keeps the same iframe and request stable across ordinary chat rerenders.
- Survives Gateway restart plus page reload without rerunning the MCP tool.
- Offers an explicit page reload when an already-open tab holds a stale process ticket or a stored view cannot be resolved.

### Plugin surface

- Native plugin manifests can declare `mcpServers`, merged through the enabled-bundle path.
- User configuration wins by server name; disabling a plugin detaches its declared server.

## Security model

- App documents and MCP metadata remain untrusted input.
- The outer sandbox has an opaque origin; the inner same-origin capability is confined to the opaque proxy document.
- App CSP origins and permissions are validated before use.
- App-initiated host requests such as `tools/call` and `ui/open-link` receive JSON-RPC method-not-found in Phase 0.
- Resource lookup requires both the process-scoped ticket and an unguessable 192-bit view ID.

## Verification

- Live Rosita/Tailscale proof with the real Excalidraw MCP App: created the OpenClaw plugin architecture diagram, kept it visible under a collapsed tool row, restarted the Gateway, reloaded the existing conversation, and recovered the same editable app without rerunning the tool.
- Live `chat.history` proof: the persisted MCP App descriptor serialized to 149 bytes and contained only `viewId`, `serverName`, `toolName`, and `resourceUri`.
- AWS Crabbox (`cbx_100691b2e58d`, `c7a.8xlarge`):
  - [436 focused tests passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_36e1d9a26aaa)
  - [final storage retention/bounds tests passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3440977bb7b5)
  - [final Chromium MCP App E2E passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_fb2774cc9f5c), including stable iframe identity, single-fetch behavior across rerenders, production CSP handshake, and reload recovery UI
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm db:kysely:check`
- focused agent, Gateway, history-projection, HTTP, UI extraction, and materialization suites
- `oxfmt` and `git diff --check`
- final `gpt-5.6-sol` autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings

## Current limit

Phase 0 is view-only for app-to-host calls. A full host bridge for app-initiated tool calls and navigation remains follow-up work.

## Release-note context

The Control UI can now render generic MCP App tool interfaces securely and restore them after reloads or Gateway restarts, while keeping large app payloads out of chat transcripts.

target.title: fix: SQLite-backed sessions never trigger byte-based auto-compaction
target.body:
Closes #104762

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where SQLite-backed sessions never trigger the `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` auto-compaction guard. Every migrated session silently falls back to token-only compaction triggering, so a session with a huge but low-token-count transcript (e.g. large tool output) never gets size-based compaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readSessionLogSnapshot` in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts` returned `{}` early for `sqlite:` session markers (the legacy JSONL tail scan is intentionally skipped for SQLite-backed transcripts), so the byte-guard path saw `undefined` transcript bytes. The SQLite marker already encodes the agent/session/store identity needed to answer this, so the fix wires that branch to `readTranscriptStatsSync(...).sizeBytes` — one accessor call, no schema changes, no behavior change for JSONL-backed sessions.

## User Impact

Users on SQLite-backed sessions (the current default) now get real byte-based auto-compaction the same way JSONL-backed sessions always have. No config changes needed.

## Evidence

- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts` — 51/51 pass, including a new regression test that seeds a real SQLite transcript and asserts compaction triggers via the `budget` reason once `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is exceeded.
- [x] Confirmed the new test fails without the fix (reverted the source change locally, test failed with `expected +0 to be 1` on `compactionCount`), then restored the fix and reran green.
- [x] `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` clean.
- [x] `codex review --uncommitted` — no actionable findings.

target.title: fix(tlon): send fragment image URLs as media
target.body:
Related: #104852

AI-assisted PR. I reviewed the diff and focused validation output.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon users sending image media URLs with fragment suffixes, such as `https://cdn.example/image.png#preview`, would have those URLs classified as ordinary links instead of image blocks.

The outbound media story path already treats plain image URLs and image URLs with query strings as image blocks. Fragment-bearing image URLs were the missing sibling case.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change keeps the fix inside Tlon's local image URL classifier by allowing the image extension check to accept either `?query` or `#fragment` suffixes.

This does not change upload behavior, URL fetching, auth, gateway routing, persisted state, migrations, schema, upgrade behavior, or non-image URL handling. It only affects the final Tlon story classification branch for URLs whose path already ends in a known image extension.

## User Impact

Tlon users can now send image URLs that include fragments and still get the expected image media block instead of a plain clickable link when the Tlon send path builds a story from that URL.

For example, `https://cdn.example/image.png#preview` now follows the same media story classification path as `https://cdn.example/image.png` and `https://cdn.example/image.png?token=1`.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the focused local probe showed the mismatch:

```text
https://cdn.example/a.png          => true
https://cdn.example/a.png?token=1  => true
https://cdn.example/a.png#preview  => false
https://cdn.example/a.webp#v=1     => false
```

The focused regression test covers `buildMediaStory("caption", "https://cdn.example/image.png#preview")` and asserts that the URL is emitted as a `block.image` story verse instead of a link verse.

Reviewer-requested live proof is still pending. ClawSweeper asked for redacted evidence from a real Tlon setup showing the upload-fallback path preserves a `.png#fragment` URL and that Tlon renders it as image media. I have not claimed that live proof yet because this machine does not currently have Tlon ship credentials, a login code, or a configured target DM/group channel available.

When a real test setup is available, the intended proof should capture this path:

```text
sendMedia(mediaUrl: "https://[redacted]/image.png#preview")
→ uploadImageFromUrl(mediaUrl)
→ upload fallback returns the original fragment URL
→ buildMediaStory(text, fallbackUrl)
→ Urbit poke payload contains block.image.src
→ Tlon UI renders the message as image media, not a plain link
```

The redacted proof should preserve the `.png#preview` shape and `block.image.src` structure while hiding ship names, login code, cookies, private hosts, request IDs, channel identifiers, and credentials.

## Possible call chain / impact

The relevant source-level fallback chain is:

```text
extensions/tlon/src/channel.runtime.ts sendMedia
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts uploadImageFromUrl
→ on upload failure, return the original imageUrl
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.ts buildMediaStory
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/story.ts isImageUrl
→ createImageBlock or createLinkInline
```

This PR only changes the Tlon-local classifier used by that story-building branch. Sibling behavior for plain image URLs, query-suffixed image URLs, upload success, auth, routing, and non-image URLs is intentionally unchanged.

## Validation

```text
git diff --check
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       3 passed (3)
```

target.title: fix(reply): suppress stranded retry after source message send
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw `message_tool_only` turns can successfully send the visible source-chat reply through `message(action=send)` and still be treated as undelivered by stranded-reply recovery. That false negative triggers the fallback: `I generated a reply but could not deliver it to this chat. Please try again.`

This PR makes source-route message-tool sends count as source-reply delivery evidence in both direct reply-agent runs and queued followup retries, while preserving stranded-retry behavior when the message tool sends only to a non-source target.

## Evidence

- Updated direct reply-agent delivery checks to treat visible message-tool sends as delivered only when they match the source route/dedupe criteria.
- Updated followup stranded-retry delivery checks with the same source-route matching, so successful source replies suppress retry diagnostics.
- Preserved retry diagnostics for sends to non-source targets.
- Targeted tests passed: `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts` (`216` tests).
- Syntax checks passed: `node --check src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` and `node --check src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts`.
- Whitespace check passed: `git diff --check`.

Note: local `pnpm tsgo:core:test` was started in the fresh worktree but produced no output for several minutes, so it was stopped rather than left hanging; CI should run the full typecheck.

target.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived embedded sessions could lose prompt-cache reuse when the same session crossed room-event delivery, sender-policy, queue, compaction, recovery, or native Responses continuation boundaries.

The failure was not one cache knob. Turn-specific delivery and authorization changed reusable prompt/tool shape, reconstructed runs could drop authoritative state, and authenticated OpenAI Responses could miss native continuation.

## What Changed

- Keeps the model-visible prompt and ordered tool catalogue stable across owner, non-owner, trusted-internal, unknown-sender, and ambient room-event turns.
- Resolves one deterministic `ToolAccessPolicy` per turn and emits a trusted full snapshot only when permissions change or model state is uncertain.
- Denies unavailable `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` calls with non-retryable `TOOL_ACCESS_DENIED` before hooks, implementations, or side effects.
- Carries immutable policy through loopback MCP grants; request headers cannot widen authority, and current-main capability/revocation checks remain intact.
- Keeps trusted-internal turns non-owner (`senderIsOwner: false`): policy can grant only the four protected core tools without exposing owner-only plugin tools.
- Separates actual reply delivery from the session-stable prompt-facing delivery mode, including `message_tool_only` room events.
- Preserves an explicit forced `message` tool on automatic Codex turns while keeping `disableMessageTool` as the hard veto.
- Propagates policy, owner identity, delivery modes, and forced snapshots through direct, queued, memory, preflight, manual, timeout, overflow, and after-turn compaction paths.
- Acknowledges policy persistence at provider-native durable boundaries for OpenClaw, Codex, and Copilot, with generation checks preventing stale acknowledgements from clearing newer state.
- Preserves native Codex supervision settings while appending trusted turn guidance as a developer history item before the user turn; no model, effort, personality, or collaboration-mode override is introduced.
- Routes built-in authenticated GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 Responses streams through native `previous_response_id` continuation with delta input. Custom streams keep their existing routing.

The earlier experimental post-history developer-message split is not included; that request shape produced HTTP 400 responses on ChatGPT/Codex Responses. Native continuation is fixed through stream classification instead.

## Security And Compatibility

- Tool visibility is not authority. Every protected call is checked again against the immutable current-turn policy immediately before execution.

Long-lived embedded sessions can lose provider prompt-cache reuse when adjacent turns cross room-event delivery, authorization, queue, compaction, recovery, or native Responses continuation boundaries.

Sanitized same-session traces showed model-visible tool inventory changing between 44 and 47 tools, prompt/tool digests changing with it, and cached prefixes collapsing to roughly 2k-10k tokens or plateauing around 37k-40k.

After stabilizing request shape, numeric-only records from a long-lived room session show the cached prefix growing from 104,960 to 157,184 tokens; the final four turns reused 98.7-99.2% of the input prefix. Three independent concerns were coupled:

1. turn-specific delivery and authorization changed reusable prompt/tool definitions;
2. reconstructed queue, memory, compaction, fallback, and recovery runs could lose authoritative state;

- Actual reply routing remains turn-specific without changing prompt-facing tool shape.
- Explicit forced `message` access survives automatic Codex turns; an explicit disable remains authoritative.
- Queue, memory, compaction, provider, and recovery boundaries preserve the same state.
- Authenticated GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 Responses use native continuation; custom streams retain their routing.
- Supervised Codex turns keep native model/effort/personality settings while receiving trusted turn guidance through append-only developer history.

target.title: fix(cli): abort reaps autonomous executor process trees
target.body:
Closes #104847

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where aborting a CLI-backed agent turn on a service-managed Gateway could stop the visible turn while leaving child processes spawned by the autonomous executor alive. Those survivors could continue acting with the executor's credentials after the operator believed the run had stopped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process supervisor now requires callers to declare a typed process role:

- `executor` runs own an independently cancellable process group on POSIX, including service-managed Gateways. If an isolated group cannot be created, startup fails closed instead of falling back to the Gateway's process group.
- `background` runs preserve the existing daemon/service ownership used by `exec`/`process` sessions and cron exit watchers that may intentionally outlive the initiating turn.

Both one-shot CLI backend runs and Claude stdio live sessions are marked as executors. The existing chat-abort path already cancels their managed run; this change makes that cancellation reach the executor's child process hierarchy without signaling the Gateway or changing persistent background-session behavior.

## User Impact

Operators can rely on abort to terminate the active CLI executor and its child process hierarchy. Persistent `exec`/`process` background sessions keep their current lifecycle and continue until they exit or are explicitly stopped.

## Evidence

PR checks for the current head (`0119396a1e`) are running with no patch-related failures at submission time: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104929/checks

Manual full CI dispatch for the same head: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29178217948

Focused coverage added:

- `src/process/supervisor/turn-lifecycle.test.ts` starts a real parent/child process hierarchy under the service-managed marker, cancels the executor run, and verifies both PIDs are gone.
- `src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts` verifies executors still receive an isolated group in service mode and cannot use the unsafe no-detach fallback.
- `src/process/supervisor/supervisor.test.ts` verifies the role is retained in run records and forwarded to the child adapter.
- `src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts` verifies both one-shot and Claude live CLI paths declare the executor role.

The preceding full run passed production types, test types, lint, core tests, CLI runner/tool shards, and agent runner shards. After rebasing onto current `main`, the fresh manual dispatch also exposed an unrelated existing `native:i18n:check` inventory drift; this PR does not touch native app or locale inventory paths. The PR-scoped CI remains the authoritative merge gate for the changed process, agent, gateway, and docs paths.

Local lightweight preflight: targeted `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, `docs:map:check` against the same ClawHub docs source used by CI, and `git diff --check` all passed. Builds and full tests were intentionally run in GitHub Actions.

## Risk And Rollback

The behavior change is limited to process-supervisor ownership for CLI executors. Windows keeps its existing tree-termination path. POSIX background work retains the existing service-managed behavior. Reverting this commit restores the previous spawn policy and removes the role contract.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve target agent tool allowlist for subagents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Spawned subagent sessions can lose tools that are allowed only on the target agent profile.

In the GBrain worker-read path, `main` can spawn `dennis-ritchie`, but `main` does not expose `gbrain_readonly`. Dennis has `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`, yet the child session inherits the parent tool allowlist before the target-agent allowlist is persisted. The result is that a fresh Dennis worker does not receive the configured read-only tool even though the target agent configuration allows it.

## Fix

When creating the initial child session patch for `spawnSubagentDirect`, merge inherited tool allow entries from:

- the caller-provided inherited allowlist
- global subagent tool allowlist config: `tools.subagents.tools.alsoAllow`
- target agent config: `targetAgentConfig.tools.alsoAllow`

This keeps the allowlist scoped to the configured target agent instead of broadening the parent or global runtime tool policy.

## Evidence

Current rebased head:

```text
fcaaf7e31139a5ca4be4de43d1b6ca1afffab50f
```

Focused verification after rebasing onto current upstream `main`:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/agents/subagent-spawn.depth-limits.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       86 passed (86)
```

Additional checks:

```text
node --check src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts
git diff --check
```

The new regression coverage exercises `main -> dennis-ritchie` where the parent inherited tool allowlist lacks `gbrain_readonly`, but Dennis' target agent config includes `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`; the persisted child session now retains `gbrain_readonly` in `inheritedToolAllow`.

## Real Runtime Reproduction

On the affected deployment after an approved gateway restart, a fresh real Dennis subagent still failed to receive the tool:

```text
Fresh Dennis subagent smoke:
- tool_search for gbrain_readonly returned 0 tools
- ALL_TOOLS had no gbrain/brain/readonly match
- stats/search/query/get_page checks could not run because the tool was absent
```

The gateway policy log for that same fresh Dennis spawn shows the exact failure mode:

```text
agents/tool-policy removed 17 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding): ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via agents.dennis-ritchie.tools.deny: web_fetch
agents/tool-policy removed 7 tool(s) via subagent tools.deny: ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via inherited tools: gbrain_readonly
```

The deployment config already grants Dennis and Albert `tools.alsoAllow` for `gbrain_readonly`, so this is not a missing config grant or plugin-load issue. The runtime is stripping the target-agent allowed tool from the child session through the inherited allowlist.

## Proof Boundary

Post-fix production proof requires this source fix to be merged/deployed and the protected gateway/runtime refresh to run. Until then, the only honest live proof available is the failure trace above plus the regression proving the fixed child-session envelope retains the target agent's configured allowlist.

## Scope

This PR is source-only. It does not deploy, change config, restart the gateway, or grant write/admin GBrain access.

target.title: fix(cron): persist startup catch-up deferrals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker now lives on `CronJobState` as `pendingCatchupDeferral`, so the existing `state_json` persistence and rollback paths own the slot and marker together. The process-local Set and its parallel rollback bookkeeping are removed. Maintenance clears the persisted marker when the slot arrives, when no valid deferred slot remains, or when the job is disabled; execution also clears it after an outcome. Existing rows need no migration because an absent field means no pending deferral.

## User Impact

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite restart path: one service starts and persists an overflow deferral, a fresh service starts 3 seconds later against the same store, the original 5-second slot survives, executes once, and clears its marker.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.startup-overflow-clobber.test.ts src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`: 3 files, 107 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.restart-catchup.test.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts`: 2 files, 81 tests passed.
- Oxlint passed for all nine changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(ai): guard payload-less media blocks from erasing tool-result text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A tool-result content block labeled `image` or `audio` with no recognizable payload causes the entire tool output to be replaced by `"(see attached image)"` — the phantom media placeholder tells the model media was attached when nothing was sent.
- **Problem**: `extractToolResultBlockText` returns `undefined` for every media-typed block regardless of payload, and `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` advertises media from payload-less husks. When a tool result contains only payload-less media blocks (no text blocks), the output degrades to `"(see attached image)"`.
- **Solution**: Add `hasMediaPayload()` and `hasInlineMediaData()` predicates. Use them in `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` and `extractToolResultBlockText` to skip/flag payload-less blocks instead of producing phantom media placeholders. Guard all provider emitters against emitting empty image blocks.
- **What changed**:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.ts` — shared helpers (hasMediaPayload, hasInlineMediaData, fixed placeholder fallback)
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts` — 18 tests
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` — emitter guard
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts` — emitter guard
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.ts` — emitter guard
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` — emitter guard
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts` — emitter guard
  - `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts` — transport emitter guard
  - `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts` — transport emitter guard
- **What did NOT change**: Session persistence, database schema, config format, public API types

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] API / contracts

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #104721
- Related #100795 (broader approach — same root cause, this PR is a focused subset)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #104721 reports that all tool results return `"(see attached image)"` literal placeholder text instead of actual output across deepseek-v4-flash and gpt-5.5 models. The root cause is that `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` and `extractToolResultBlockText` in the shared `tool-result-text.ts` treat every media-typed content block as genuine media, even when it carries no payload. A payload-less media block (from session corruption, plugin bugs, or older sessions) causes the tool result text to vanish and be replaced with a media placeholder.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Tool results with payload-less media blocks no longer degrade to phantom media placeholders
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/media-payload-guard-104721`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)

$ pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  68 passed (68)

$ pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  43 passed (43)
```

**Matrix-style evidence (before vs after)**:

| Scenario | Input | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phantom image replaces output | `[{type:"image"}]` (no data) | `extractToolResultText` → `""` → output becomes `"(see attached image)"` | `extractToolResultText` → `"[image omitted: missing payload]"` |
| Phantom audio replaces output | `[{type:"audio"}]` (no data) | Same, `"(see attached audio)"` | `"[audio omitted: missing payload]"` |
| Text + phantom image | `[{type:"text",text:"real output"},{type:"image"}]` | `"real output"` (text preserved) but emitter sends empty image block | `"real output"` + emitter skips empty image |
| Genuine image (unchanged) | `[{type:"image",data:"img"}]` | `undefined` (media path) / `"(see attached image)"` | Same ✅ |
| Text block with image mime | `[{type:"text",text:"hello",mimeType:"image/png"}]` | False image detection → `"(see attached image)"` | No false detection → `undefined` ✅ |
| hasInlineMediaData | `{type:"image",data:"img"}` | N/A (new function) | `true` ✅ |
| hasInlineMediaData | `{type:"image"}` (no data) | N/A (new function) | `false` ✅ |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `extractToolResultText` returns `"[image omitted: missing payload]"` for payload-less image-only content instead of empty string
  2. `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` returns `undefined` for payload-less media blocks instead of `"(see attached image)"`
  3. Text blocks with image-like mime metadata no longer trigger false image detection
  4. Mixed text + payload-less-image content correctly returns the text
  5. Provider-native emitters skip payload-less image blocks instead of emitting empty image URLs / base64 data
- What was not tested: Live end-to-end provider API calls (guarded by the same pattern in converters + unit tests)

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**
  - ✅ Auth guard: N/A — no permission/policy changes
  - ✅ Enum completeness: `hasMediaPayload` covers all canonical wire shapes (data, url, file_id, image_url string/object, source.data/url, input_audio, audio); `hasInlineMediaData` covers inline base64
  - ✅ Path coverage: Shared helpers (`describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder`, `extractToolResultBlockText`) + all 5 provider emitters + 2 transport streams use the same guards
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Payload-less media blocks get a fixed placeholder text, not JSON stringification (which could leak nested payload-shaped fields)

## Root Cause

Payload-less media-typed content blocks (e.g. `{ type: "image", mimeType: "image/png" }` without `data`) suppress text extraction and advertise phantom media. The shared functions in `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-result-text.ts` trusted the type label alone — no payload verification existed.

## Regression Test Plan

All 18 existing + new tests pass. Broader provider tests (anthropic 68, openai-completions 43, google-shared 12) also pass unchanged.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Tool results with payload-less media blocks show `"[image omitted: missing payload]"` instead of `"(see attached image)"`
- All other behavior unchanged

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the shared `tool-result-text.ts` is the correct boundary for text extraction; all provider emitters also need the inline-data guard to prevent invalid API payloads
- **Refactor needed**: No — targeted 9-file change with consistent pattern across all emitters
- **Alternative considered**: Shared-helper-only approach (commit 1) — fixed text extraction but didn't prevent emitters from sending empty image blocks. Expanded to cover emitters after ClawSweeper review (commit 2)

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: A payload-less media block from a genuine source (e.g. plugin that intentionally sends empty media) now renders as `"[image omitted: missing payload]"` text instead of `"(see attached image)"`. This is strictly better — the model gets a readable explanation rather than a misleading "image was attached" message.

**Mitigation**: Backward compatible for genuine media (blocks with `data`/`url`/`file_id` payloads are unaffected). The change only affects payload-less blocks that were already broken (producing incorrect placeholder text).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

---

target.title: fix(browser): check own profile entries for profile operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser profile names are user-controlled config keys. Inherited object properties such as `constructor` and `prototype` were treated as real profile entries in several create, delete, projection, hot-reload, and gateway patch paths. A valid profile with one of those names could therefore be rejected, omitted, or fail to round-trip.

Live route testing also exposed an adjacent deletion failure: when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` or `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` placed Browser state outside the OS home/temp roots, deleting a launched profile returned HTTP 500 because the trash helper rejected Browser's own configured state directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use own-property checks at every Browser profile lookup boundary.
- Preserve valid top-level profile keys while continuing to strip nested prototype-pollution keys from untrusted config patches.
- Keep profile listing and hot reload consistent with persisted config.
- Authorize trash moves only from Browser's owned `<config>/browser` subtree. Existing realpath, symlink-escape, target-identity, and trash-destination checks remain in force; the wider config directory is not authorized.

## User Impact

Profiles named `constructor` or `prototype` can be created, listed, hot-reloaded, patched, and deleted normally. Custom state directories outside the home directory work without granting Browser deletion authority over unrelated config or filesystem paths.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `194d41eab680c1964c70087a60e03df607470878`
- Exact GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29032054298 - passed.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox: lease `cbx_7b2824bafef4`, run `run_231cff1f9ccb`; public networking, no Tailscale, no instance profile, IMDSv2 IAM endpoint 404, exact head verified, Node 24.15 / pnpm 11.2.2; 180 focused tests passed. Lease released.
- Native `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 101694` - passed at the exact PR head.
- Fresh autoreview at the exact head - clean, confidence 0.91.
- Real Express route proof: create and delete `constructor` through `POST /profiles/create` and `DELETE /profiles/constructor`; persistence round-tripped and `Object.prototype` remained unchanged.
- Real Gateway RPC proof: `config.patch` created and removed the profile while nested `constructor` / `prototype` payload keys remained stripped.
- Custom-state route proof: launched/stopped profile deletion under a configured state directory outside home/temp succeeds; unrelated config subtrees, root config authority, and symlink escapes remain rejected.

Live Dev Gateway + OpenAI agent + Browser proof will be added before merge; it is intentionally not claimed by the current evidence.

### 2026-07-12 follow-up: exact-head local proof

- Exact PR head verified locally: `ca0e4b3eff432c1c77cf5ae1810712c9e7570668`.

target.title: fix(openai): redact token refresh error response body
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex OAuth token refresh reads the full error response body via `response.text()` on failed requests with no size limit and no redaction. Secrets in error responses (e.g. `refresh_token` in `error_description`) are exposed in the error message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `response.text()` with `extractProviderErrorDetail` ? the canonical bounded provider error helper ? so error body consumption is capped at 16 KiB and sensitive values are redacted.

Matches the merged Chutes OAuth fix ([#103569](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103569)): `readResponseTextLimited` ? `assertOkOrThrowProviderError`, with secret redaction tests.

## User Impact

**Before:** unbounded error body read, secrets in error responses logged
**After:** bounded at 16 KiB via `extractProviderErrorDetail`, secrets redacted

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** OpenAI OAuth token refresh/authorization failures read unbounded response bodies and embed raw provider error text; the fix caps error body reads at 16 KiB and redacts sensitive values (refresh_token, access_token) from returned failure messages.

**Real environment tested:** Windows 11, Node.js v24.18.0, openclaw commit `8201b1c3` on branch `fix/openai-oauth-refresh-error-body`.

**Steps run after the patch:**
```
// Live loopback proof ? exercises extractProviderErrorDetail against real HTTP server
node --import tsx scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts

// Full-chain regression tests ? exercises postTokenForm ? readResponseWithLimit ? extractProviderErrorDetail
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix:**
```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts

=== #103578 bounded OAuth error proof ===

Case 1 ? secret redacted from error body: PASS
Case 2 ? oversized body bounded: PASS
Case 3 ? normal body preserved: PASS

OVERALL: ALL PASSED
```

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

**Observed result after fix:** The loopback proof exercises `extractProviderErrorDetail` against a real HTTP server with realistic OAuth error responses containing `refresh_token` and `access_token` fields ? secret values are redacted, oversized bodies are capped at 16 KiB, and normal error text is preserved. The regression tests exercise the full production `postTokenForm` ? `readResponseWithLimit` ? `refreshAccessToken`/`exchangeAuthorizationCode` chain via mocked SSRF, confirming both callers return bounded, redacted failure messages.

**What was not tested:** A live OAuth flow against the real `auth.openai.com` endpoint could not be executed because it requires a valid OpenAI OAuth client_id/client_secret pair (not available to external contributors). The loopback proof exercises the same production `extractProviderErrorDetail` function with realistic error payloads; the runtime tests exercise the same `postTokenForm` production path with bounded response reading and the same caller-level redaction logic.

## Diff summary

```
extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.ts      | 18 +/-
extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts | 101 ++++
scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts                 |  89 ++++
```

target.title: Instrument native hook relay fan-out
target.body:
## Summary
- add per-registration native hook relay metrics for command requests and real invocations
- log aggregate relay summaries at unregister with event counts, total/max duration, and no-local-work command requests
- warn on slow native hook relay invocations (>=250ms) with relay/session/tool context

## What Problem This Solves
Operators observed short, high-CPU bursts from `openclaw-hooks` workers during normal Telegram/Codex activity. Source inspection points at Codex native hook relay fan-out as a likely hot path: the Codex harness can register native events such as `pre_tool_use`, `post_tool_use`, `permission_request`, and `before_agent_finalize`; when local work exists, those events cross a process boundary through `openclaw hooks relay`.

The important next step is observability, not behavior change. This PR adds low-noise aggregate metrics around the native hook relay path so operators can confirm which relay events are requested, which ones actually invoke OpenClaw work, how long they take, and whether no-local-work requests are still contributing to fan-out.

This PR does not change relay behavior, approval semantics, hook policy, or gateway configuration.

## Evidence
Redacted live host observations from the OpenClaw hook-burst investigation:

- 2026-07-06 hook-cost audit: short-lived `openclaw-hooks` workers were observed around 145-175% CPU during normal Telegram/OpenClaw use, with CPU temperature near 97C in one snapshot. A later audit snapshot reproduced one `openclaw-hooks` worker around 159% CPU while CPU temperature was 83.6C.
- Controlled local timing sample after a temporary operator-only runtime timing patch on OpenClaw 2026.6.11: 19 native relay invocations in roughly 40 seconds, including 10 `pre_tool_use` calls at 1-54ms and 9 `post_tool_use` calls at 0-1ms. No `>=250ms` slow relay lines appeared in that short sample, which suggests the burst problem is likely process fan-out/overlap rather than one slow handler.
- During that same sample, a short-lived `openclaw-hooks` worker was observed around 163% CPU and disappeared within seconds.
- 2026-07-06 post-restart memory watch: pre-restart gateway cgroup memory was about 2.5GB, gateway node RSS about 887MB, swap effectively full, and another short-lived `openclaw-hooks` burst hit about 166% CPU. Immediately after restart, another short-lived hook worker hit about 157% CPU during the first post-restart turn.
- 2026-07-06 workload checkpoint after starting a real Symphony/Codex review lane: gateway cgroup memory rose to about 7.0GB with 584 tasks while gateway node RSS stayed under about 1GB; two short-lived `openclaw-hooks` workers were observed around 162-163% CPU, with multiple Codex app-server workers active under the gateway cgroup. This points at child-process fan-out/worker overlap rather than a single gateway heap-only leak.
- 2026-07-08 follow-up inspection: gateway cgroup memory was about 5.6GB, cgroup peak about 9.1GB, 417 tasks, swap about 7.3GB/8GB used, 8 resident Codex app-server wrapper/native pairs, and a short-lived `openclaw-hooks` worker around 170% CPU / 340MB RSS while inspecting.

Source-level findings from the same investigation:

- The live config did not explicitly set `nativeHookRelay`; the Codex harness enabled native hook relay by default.
- `post_tool_use` and `before_agent_finalize` are locally gated by whether matching global hooks exist, but once local work exists, the relay still crosses a process boundary.
- The generic void-hook path runs matching hook work in parallel, so several short-lived relay processes can overlap during tool-heavy turns.

## Relation To #101099
#101099 was an earlier timing-instrumentation lane from the same investigation. This PR is the cleaner/narrower aggregate-metrics lane:

- #101099 focused on timing logs from an operator patch direction.
- #102241 adds source-level per-registration counters, no-local-work request counts, aggregate unregister summaries, and slow-invocation warnings in one relay file.

If maintainers prefer one observability shape, this PR should supersede or narrow #101099 rather than both landing independently.

## Verification
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (13/13)
- `TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-native-relay-test-XXXXXX) node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (80/80)

Note: the same relay test without isolated `TMPDIR` can see a live gateway native-hook bridge record in the shared OS temp dir and fail its PID-isolation expectation; isolating `TMPDIR` avoids that host-local interference.

target.title: fix(agents): keep subagent run ID mask from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the subagent run-ID mask used in lifecycle log/error metadata could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the run ID contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`maskRunId` sliced its prefix/suffix with raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the masked ID always falls on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The helper was also moved to module scope and exported so it can be unit-tested directly.

## User Impact

Subagent lifecycle warnings and error metadata remain well-formed when run IDs contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Moved `maskRunId` to module scope in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` and exported it.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` covering ASCII masking and astral boundary cases.
- Existing lifecycle controller tests continue to pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a run ID like `"abc😀xxxxxxxxx"` produced `"abc\ud83d…\ude00xxxx"` (isolated surrogate halves). After the patch it returns `"abc…xxxx"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/mask-runid-utf16` at `71f75fbfa526d0041851c3530662325cc35ac424`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; for (const v of ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b", "short"]) console.log(JSON.stringify(maskRunId(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the masked values survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mr-")), "m.txt"); const samples = ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b"]; const masked = samples.map(maskRunId); writeFileSync(f, masked.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === masked.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  "run-…7890"
  "abc…xxxx"
  "xxxx…abc"
  "***"

  run-…7890
  abc…xxxx
  xxxx…abc
  ***
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at mask boundaries` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every masked value, no isolated surrogates are emitted, and the joined masked values survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live subagent lifecycle failure path; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

_AI-assisted PR: changes and tests were generated with AI assistance and manually reviewed._

target.title: fix(diagnostics): derive heap thresholds from V8 heap size limit (#104631)
target.body:
Closes #104631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the gateway with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` above the default (e.g. 8 GB on a 15 GB RAM host) receive false-positive `heap_threshold` critical memory pressure diagnostics as soon as `heapUsedBytes` reaches 2 GB, even when the V8 heap limit has 75%+ headroom and the system has abundant free memory.

This triggers unnecessary diagnostic events, log noise, and stability bundle writes, and can cause downstream monitoring or supervisor restart chains (the linked issue reports a gateway drain-and-restart sequence on the reporter's setup).

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic memory classifier previously hardcoded heap pressure thresholds at 1 GiB (warning) and 2 GiB (critical) — values that were reasonable for Node's default `--max-old-space-size` (~2 GB server / ~4 GB desktop) but do not scale when operators configure a larger heap limit.

This change derives default heap warning and critical thresholds from V8's effective `heap_size_limit`, so they automatically adapt to whatever `--max-old-space-size` is set:

- **Critical**: 75% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 2 GiB
- **Warning**: 60% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 1 GiB

The conservative lower bounds ensure small-heap or default-heap environments remain equally protected. RSS threshold and RSS growth detection are unchanged. No configuration key is added — the fix is fully automatic.

## User Impact

Users on decently-provisioned hosts (e.g. `--max-old-space-size=8192`) no longer see spurious `heap_threshold` critical pressure from routine heap usage at 2 GB, while the same protection level is preserved for default or constrained heap sizes. The change is invisible to operators: no new config, no migration, no restart requirement beyond the usual update.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

3 new focused tests, 14 total, all passing (99 tests across 3 diagnostic suites):

| Test | What it proves |
|------|---------------|
| `default heap thresholds never go below the original constants as a conservative lower bound (#104631)` | Adaptive defaults floor at 1 GiB / 2 GiB — small-heap protection unchanged |
| `emits heap_threshold at the adaptive default warning threshold (#104631)` | Warning fires at 60% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |
| `emits heap_threshold critical at the adaptive default critical threshold (#104631)` | Critical fires at 75% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |

All tests call the exported `emitDiagnosticMemorySample()` without a `thresholds` override, exercising the real default path that the gateway heartbeat uses.

### Real-behavior proof

A standalone harness exercises the production adaptive-threshold computation and real `process.memoryUsage()` sampling across three isolated subprocesses with different `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` configurations. Each subprocess calls `v8.getHeapStatistics()` and `process.memoryUsage()` — the same APIs the gateway heartbeat uses — and reports the computed thresholds and current memory state.

**Default V8 heap limit (~4.19 GB):**
```
limit=4.19 GB  w=2.51 GB  c=3.14 GB
heap=0.00 GB  => none
floor_warning=PASS (1.00 GB)  floor_critical=PASS (2.00 GB)
2.5 GB heap: old=critical/hardcoded_2GB  new=no (adaptive 3.14 GB)
```
The 2.5 GB heap case that would have triggered critical under the old hardcoded threshold is now correctly classified as no pressure.

**Enlarged heap (max-old-space-size=8192, matching reporter's ~8 GB environment):**
```
limit=8.19 GB  w=4.91 GB  c=6.14 GB
heap=0.00 GB  => none
floor_warning=PASS (1.00 GB)  floor_critical=PASS (2.00 GB)
2.5 GB heap: old=critical/hardcoded_2GB  new=no (adaptive 6.14 GB)
```
The false-positive critical at 2 GB is eliminated. The adaptive threshold correctly scales to 6.14 GB.

**Constrained heap (max-old-space-size=1024, ~1.19 GB):**
```
limit=1.19 GB  w=1.00 GB  c=2.00 GB
heap=0.00 GB  => none
floor_warning=PASS (1.00 GB)  floor_critical=PASS (2.00 GB)
2.5 GB heap: old=critical/hardcoded_2GB  new=yes
```
The conservative floor ensures thresholds never drop below the original 1 GiB / 2 GiB safety net.

**Typecheck**: `tsgo:core` passes clean.

**Lint**: `oxlint` zero errors.

**98 existing tests** in the diagnostic logging suite remain green (no collateral damage).

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.
